candidates.reason: The key judgments for whether there is valid consideration for the contract variation promise include Williams v Roffey Bros (J32) which established that a practical benefit can constitute good consideration for a promise of extra payment even for existing duties, provided there is no duress or fraud. Stilk v Myrick (J31) presents the traditional rule denying such consideration, which Williams refined rather than overruled. Central London Property Trust v High Trees (J33) is also relevant for principles of modification and estoppel. Dunlop Pneumatic Tyre Co v New Garage (J48) is important regarding liquidated damages context parallel to this case. Balfour v Balfour (J29) provides contrast on intention to create legal relations but is less directly related to consideration in contract variation.

candidates.reason: For enforcing Castlegate's promise on promissory estoppel grounds, Central London Property Trust v High Trees (J33) is the leading case establishing promissory estoppel principles. Williams v Roffey Bros (J32) can also support some estoppel reasoning though it is primarily about consideration. Stilk v Myrick (J31) is relevant as contrasting position pre-estoppel development. Dunlop (J48) and Balfour (J29) are less directly relevant but can be cited either for context or to distinguish intention to be bound or penalty clauses.
